title: Research: exact star-decoder hierarchies, target budgets, and COPY bounds
head: 8f4600b41bf1f0f5d07f209e5d3950eb22ef5cad
body:
This research contribution determines sharp information thresholds for signed proper-star decoders and proves physical COPY obstructions for explicitly defined classes. It adds uniform proofs, exact prescribed-target criteria, and independent finite certificates. **There is no new multiplication coefficient or claimed physical supplier.**

For `q=p-k>=3`, the first five generalized weights are now exactly
`(2q+2,4q+3,6q+3,8q+2,10q)`. At the boundary `q=2,k>=4`, an affine cube gives `(6,11,14,15,16)`: three, four, or five selectable targets all require eleven deletions. These deletion counts measure information recovery; the physical notes separately charge copied frame dimensions and inherited endpoint schedules.

### Results and review entry points

Only `research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/` changes. Start with its README.

- **Uniform higher weights:** `HIGHER-WEIGHTS.md`, `FOURTH-WEIGHT.md`, and `FIFTH-WEIGHT.md` prove the first five weights for every `k>=2,q>=3`. Every second-weight word is a sum of two adjacent minimum stars. Every rank-three and rank-four optimum is a star clique; every rank-five optimum is a five-star clique for `q>=4`. The notes give exact counts and prescribed-target independence criteria. The `q=3` rank-five equality classification remains open.
- **Exceptional cube geometry:** `CUBE-OPTIMIZERS.md` proves exact ordinary-cube shortening and classifies all rank-three through rank-five optima for `q=2,k>=4`. Prescribed target sets of those sizes attain eleven deletions exactly when they use the same original pairs and have affinely independent signs.
- **Arbitrary graph targets:** `HIGHER-GRAPH.md` gives the complete `k=2` generalized-weight hierarchies. `GRAPH-TARGETS.md` adds exact partition formulations for arbitrary target sets, a capacity-matching formula for every forest in the nonempty-star code, and every prescribed triple budget in both codes. These results go beyond choosing a favorable target set.
- **Core shortening:** `CORE-SHORTENING.md` identifies the full unrestricted-sign shortening on `k-2` original pairs at `q=3`, its exact dimension, and the sharp weight-sixteen threshold of the additional polynomial layers. Simply repeating the fixed-sign graph code omits these layers.
- **Recoding and sequential copying obstruction:** `COPY-OBSTRUCTION.md` proves that an integral separating pairing with odd diagonal forces total copied frame rank `C>=v`, including arbitrary linear observation recodings, exact nonlinear postprocessing, individually readable corrections, and chronological copy-to-zero innovations under the stated monotone-frame model. Every even-size paired-port geometry with overlap-one readability satisfies the hypothesis. The inherited odd-stage ledger then has no positive deficit. The selected E8 geometry has even diagonal and is outside this result.
- **Native odd-star cost:** `ODD-NATIVE-COST.md` proves a bit-saving ceiling `c<107/66606` for every odd `k>=5` in the inherited schedule with at least five stages, accounting for source/target climbs, idle hosting, and whole banks even while granting other work free. A separately stated conditional three-stage extension excludes odd `k>=7`. Both ceilings are below the campaign-start selected coefficient. Arbitrary recoding and COPY-assisted innovations are outside this particular theorem.

Earlier uniform minimum-word rigidity, all optimal two-dimensional subcodes, and exact prescribed-pair budgets remain included. A generalized weight `d_r` yields `d_r-r` deletions for **some selectable r-target set**, not every prescribed set. Code statements cover both proper-star spaces; the original uniform overlap corrections are absorbed only at power-of-two `k`.

### Reproduction and evidence

Python 3.10+; standard library only:

```sh
for check in shortening optimizer block copy_obstruction core_shortening graph_targets; do
  python3 -I -O -B "research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/${check}_verify.py" --self-test || exit
done
for check in higher cube boundary; do
  python3 -I -O -B "research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/${check}_verify.py" --self-test || exit
done
python3 -I -O -B research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/global_verify.py --self-test
python3 -I -O -B research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/verify.py --negative-controls
```

The current campaign checkers cover 42 full-generator cube shortenings; all 187 relevant `RM(1,4)` subspaces and 6,748 target sets; complete small complementary-block models; eight exact binary/rational COPY matrix cases and a sequential-innovation fragment; full-generator original-core shortenings at `k=3,...,6` with all 1,048,576 words of the smallest code; and 4,112 complete graph target sets plus 73 triple/quadruple orbits covering 12,650 sets at `p=4`. The graph oracle directly checks 4,329,472 decoder assignments. Receipts distinguish exhaustive domains, overlapping case instances, and logical meet-in-the-middle candidate counts.

All six campaign self-tests passed isolated optimized execution, relocation, corruption rejection and failure-output preservation. The graph checker also tests atomic replacement failure cleanup. Proofs and implementations received separate AI-assisted reviews; the lead reviewed the resulting proofs and code. Earlier higher-target receipts were reproduced under Python 3.11.13 and 3.14.5; campaign receipts currently record Python 3.14.5. No human or proof-assistant verification is claimed. Finite enumeration supports the separate uniform proofs. Selected supplier cold replay, unrelated regeneration, and hosted CI are not claimed.

### Provenance and remaining work

Original base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Campaign continuation base: `7d526020fc368ce4157cd436995c2f4fcf683318`. Latest inspected main snapshot: `007664306fff84fbb1c9a1b4053b69f439764034`, whose selected record and actual #890 integration review report conditional κ `1661957774647029/10^18`; its #589-on-#555 bit supplier is unchanged. `upstream/` and selected certificates are untouched. Seed **48**, structural decoder research.

Credit **Luke Mansoor (#732)** for uniform minimum distance, **Sagar Thakrar (#725)** for the `q=1` exception, **Alishan Ladhani (#747)** for the finite `(6,4)` minimum-word classification, **ellipsi2 (#772)** for uniform ranks, and **Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (#231)** with **icekylinx/eumemic** for the paired-cube decoder lineage. The graph incidence-code/cut bridge is credited to Martínez-Bernal, Valencia-Bucio, and Villarreal, [arXiv:1812.04106v2, Corollary 2.13](https://arxiv.org/html/1812.04106v2). Physical notes retain the inherited odd-stage/hosting and rank-product credits and immutable source pins.

Overlap was refreshed through #958. **Ross Richardson's #958** studies a distinct five-port point-only decoder with quadratic labels and both overlap-one and overlap-three corrections; our native odd-star result uses incidence labels, additional proper-star observations, and overlap-one corrections. #939/#954 concern E8 geometry outside our integral odd-diagonal hypothesis. No literature-wide priority claim is made.

`CAMPAIGN-18H.json` records the active minimum eighteen-hour campaign, reviewed milestones, exact receipts and remaining obligations. The present checkpoint does not complete that campaign. Higher-rank classification, remaining odd-size observation classes, and fully priced source/helper/frame/restoration/recursive schedules remain under investigation. No deletion count is promoted to a physical supplier invoice.
